question: All right, well, let's start with you Mr. Dal Col. What I was wondering, in seeing some of the debate, why did Rick Lazio really make this race about Bill Clinton? Hillary Clinton didn't run for president.
answer: Well, what you've got to look at it is Mrs. Clinton has no record, she's never voted for anything, never put any legislation in. She kept pointing to 30 years of work, which is interesting, but she failed to point out that most of it was in Arkansas. So what Rick had to do is demonstrate the fact that he's got a record, that he can provide leadership, that he'll be the senator from New York who will fight for the voters in New York. I think Rick did that, I think it was a lively debate. I think the voters got a look -- good look at both candidates and they can start to make up their mind now.

question: Well, what they saw was this dramatic moment where he decided to take this pledge and walk it over to Mrs. Clinton and ask her to pledge not to take any more soft money. Why the strategy behind that?
answer: Well, what you've got a look at is Mrs. Clinton has run her campaign largely since June on soft money. There have been over 10 negative ads attacking Rick, distorting his record, paid for with soft money. She says she's for campaign finance reform, we've not set up any kind of a up to joint committee as she has, we've taken no soft money. It's time to put on the line. Can you trust her? Can you trust what she says? Will she do it she says? And I think answer clearly the voters of New York so far is no.
